main.description: The standing prose on a Ratioed piece's page, kept as a record so it can be rewritten without a deploy — the same reason the post template is a record rather than a constant. A singleton at rkey "self". Every field is optional and every one has a built-in default: an absent field is not an empty caption, it is the sentence the site ships with. Nothing here is a measurement. The figures, the counts, the reaction time and the log are read from the piece's own record and cannot be edited from this one; what this holds is the writing around them, which is the artist's and drifts as the project's own account of itself does.

liveLede.description: The opening paragraph of a piece that is still up. {take} is substituted with the take number. A piece with its own `lede` on its record overrides this, as it does the generated one.

liveNote.description: Under the live dashboard: what the page will do when the piece ends.

deckAlive.description: What the dashboard says while nobody has liked it.

deckLiked.description: What it says once somebody has, which is the moment the piece is over and the reaction time is running.

deckWithdrawn.description: What it says when a like was cast and taken back, and nothing is standing against the piece.

deckStream.description: What the reader's browser is doing while the firehose is on. {budget} is substituted with the megabyte cap the stream stops itself at.

deckRecord.description: The same, while the deck is reading the piece's own record instead.

replay.description: Over the replay of a finished piece.

witnessed.description: Over the log the studio kept while the piece ran, inside the folded panel.

roster.description: Over the faces of everyone who was there.

hidden.description: Over the replies written into a thread the threadgate had already closed.

log.description: Over the measured event log. The sentence about how many breaking likes have since been deleted is appended by the site and counted from the records, not written here.

reach.description: Under the reach table, explaining what the score is. The site appends what it could not resolve and the date the follower counts were read.
